author: Mistress Helga Thornwort, apothecary

#To the Beginner

Alchemy is the art of coaxing hidden virtues out of plants, fungi, bones and stranger things. Every ingredient carries several such virtues, and two ingredients that share a virtue can be combined into a potion that has it.

That is the whole art, really. The rest is practice, patience and a strong stomach.

#Learning What an Ingredient Does

The simplest way to learn an ingredient's first virtue is to taste it. The second, third and fourth virtues reveal themselves only through experiment: mixing it with others and seeing what happens.

Taste with care. Some mushrooms cure the cough. Others cure the condition of being alive.

#My Favourite Ingredients for Beginners

Blue mountain flowers are common and restore health. Wheat restores health too, and is easy to find near any farm. Butterfly wings help with both. Mixing any two of these will give you a weak healing draught, and every potion you make teaches you something.

For stamina, look for certain mushrooms that grow in caves and the meat of small river creatures. For magicka, many of the pale and glowing flowers will serve.

#Poisons

A good alchemist knows poisons as well as cures. Nightshade, deathbell and certain fungi grow in dark places and make potent toxins. Apply them to a blade, not to your supper.

Store your poisons on a separate shelf from your potions. I learned this the hard way, and so did my former apprentice.

#A Final Tip

Visit an alchemy lab whenever you can. A proper set of retorts, mortar and alembic makes all the difference. And sell your extra potions: merchants pay well, and coin buys rarer ingredients.
